Subject: Renewal: Premium support & SLO uplift

Hi Grace,

We're coming up on our July renewal and the execs want to lock in a premium support path for Q3–Q4. Two asks from our side: a) a firm latency SLO for 99th percentile tail under committed throughput (we're targeting a 95% reduction in tail errors during peak); and b) a committed capacity uplift (+30% baseline throughput with burst access).

Attached is our Q1 usage extract so you can see current patterns. Can you share what a mutual action plan looks like, high-level pricing delta for the premium SLA, and what timelines are reasonable for deployment/test? We're hoping to finalize by the end of next week so procurement can start paperwork.

Thanks,
Paul Whitman
Head of Platform
Orbit Cloud

Subject: Re: Renewal: Premium support & SLO uplift

Paul —

Thanks for the note and the usage file. We can absolutely support both asks; the usual flow we recommend is:

- Draft a short MAP (mutual action plan) that captures deliverables, timing, and acceptance criteria (I attached a short draft).
- Lock a committed throughput number and specify burst allowances. That lets us size Dedicated capacity or a reserved pool.
- Define the SLO targets (eg. 99th < 350ms for the public endpoint with the agreed throughput) and a rollback/fallback model (auto-route to compatible model variant if SLOs breached).

High-level timeline: 2 business days to confirm MAP and committed throughput, 3–5 business days to provision a staging pool and run acceptance tests, and then a contract amendment for renewal (DocuSign) to sign the SLA table.

I'll loop in Marissa for pricing and ben for operational oncall handoff. Proposed times for a quick 30-min sync tomorrow: 10:00am or 2:00pm PT. Which works?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Paul —

Following Grace's MAP draft, attaching the premium SLA term sheet and a redline-friendly summary of pricing. Key points:

- Premium SLA: 4-hour P1 response, 24/7 on-call escalation, and a 99th percentile latency SLO target defined per endpoint. We propose the 99th target at 350ms under the committed throughput of 120k tokens/min (baseline +30% from current).
- Capacity & billing: committed monthly throughput billed as reserved units; burst is metered at a discounted overage rate.
- Credits & remedies: we include a non-disruptive rollback policy and financial credit table for repeated SLO breaches (outlined in section 3).
- Term & pricing: annual renewal with a 12% uplift in unit price for the premium package; first year discounted to 8% for a multi-year commit.

DocuSign link for the amendment: https://www.docusign.com/templates/REDWOOD-SLA-8472
Attachment: redwood-premium-sla-term-sheet.pdf (pdf)

If this looks reasonable I'm happy to send a draft amendment to procurement and route to legal. Grace — can you confirm the staging test windows and an acceptance test harness we'll run against Orbit's traffic shape? Ben — please prep a quick oncall roster + escalation playbook if we move forward.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
